source_name: RTVSLO / MMC — public broadcaster news portal
why_relevant: Free, archive-stable national coverage of procurement disputes and state-sector contracts; useful open substitute where Finance/Delo/Večer are paywalled.

source_name: MojeDelo.com – slovenski zaposlitveni portal (oglasi za delo)
why_relevant: Largest Slovenian job board; bank and vendor postings for roles such as 'vodja projekta uvedbe plačilnega sistema', 'core banking migracija', 'SEPA/instant payments specialist' reveal an awarded or imminent implementation contract months before (or instead of) any tender/award publication. Job text usually names the technology stack, which identifies the vendor.

source_name: Optius.com – zaposlitveni portal, področje Informatika/Programiranje
why_relevant: Second major SI job board with a dedicated IT category and per-company pages (e.g. NLB, OTP banka). Company pages act as a longitudinal hiring feed per bank — a burst of integration/testing roles is a reliable proxy for a running implementation programme.

source_name: Zaposlitev.si – job board
why_relevant: Third general SI job board named in the cell brief; adds coverage for postings syndicated by staffing agencies acting for banks/vendors, which sometimes name the project even when the bank does not.

source_name: Zavod RS za zaposlovanje (ESS) – objave prostih delovnih mest / iskanje dela
why_relevant: Official national employment service. Public-sector and state-owned employers are LEGALLY REQUIRED to publish vacancies here — which covers state-owned banks/insurers and public bodies procuring payment services. This makes it the most complete and least-gamed hiring feed for the public half of the market.

source_name: NLB Group – Prosta delovna mesta (careers)
why_relevant: Largest banking group in Slovenia/SEE. First-party vacancy feed; group-level postings expose regional roll-out programmes (one contract, many markets) that never surface in a Slovenian tender portal.

source_name: SID banka – Prosta delovna mesta
why_relevant: State-owned development bank; a public-law entity whose IT/payments hires (e.g. 'specialist za plačilni promet') pair directly with its obligation to run public procurement, letting hiring be cross-referenced against eJN award notices.

source_name: Deželna banka Slovenije – Zaposlitve
why_relevant: Smaller private SI bank; exactly the profile whose vendor deals are never announced. Its careers page is often the only public trace of a system change.

source_name: LinkedIn – Slovenia bank/payments jobs and employee posts
why_relevant: Best source for English-titled implementation roles ('core banking migration lead', 'Temenos/Flexcube consultant, Ljubljana') and for vendor employees publicly celebrating a go-live at a named Slovenian bank — frequently the earliest public confirmation of a private-sector award.

source_name: Careerjet Slovenia – job aggregator (per-company views)
why_relevant: Aggregator that pulls postings from many SI boards and corporate ATS pages into one searchable per-company view — an efficient discovery layer to find WHICH boards a given bank/vendor actually uses, which can then be monitored directly.

source_name: Dnevi slovenske informatike (DSI) – conference programme, Slovensko društvo INFORMATIKA
why_relevant: The flagship Slovenian IT conference (33rd edition, 14–15 April 2026). Session titles and speaker affiliations are effectively a public register of live projects: a bank IT director and a vendor co-presenting a 'digital wallet' or payments platform case study is a disclosed implementation. Yearly per-edition subdomains give a stable historical archive back to at least 2022.

source_name: Slovensko društvo INFORMATIKA – dogodki (events listing)
why_relevant: Parent association that announces DSI and other professional IT events; the events section is a pointer to each year's conference site and to smaller specialist gatherings where bank IT staff speak.

source_name: Združenje bank Slovenije (ZBS) – Bančna konferenca / sporočila za javnost
why_relevant: The Slovenian Bank Association's annual Bančna konferenca (e.g. 3 June 2026, Brdo pri Kranju, on digital sovereignty and EU payment infrastructure) plus its press-release stream carry sector-level statements on payment-infrastructure programmes — the framing that precedes bank-level procurement. Its instant-payments regulation notice is an example of a shared programme with many downstream contracts.

source_name: ZBS – Strokovna izobraževanja (professional training/seminar calendar)
why_relevant: Seminar and 'posvet' topics (e.g. for zakladniki, poravnava, skrbniške storitve) track what banks are being made to implement next; a sudden training block on a new payment scheme or reporting standard is a leading indicator of vendor spend across all member banks at once.

source_name: Bančni vestnik – revija za denarništvo in bančništvo (ZBS)
why_relevant: Only Slovenian monthly banking journal (since 1951), with an English international issue each November. Practitioner articles authored by bank IT/payments staff routinely describe systems being introduced and name the platform — an author affiliation map doubles as an actor map for the cell.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. – novice, letna poročila, shema Flik
why_relevant: The national card/payment processor for all Slovenian banks and operator of the instant-payment settlement scheme (Flik, live since Feb 2019). Its news and annual reports disclose infrastructure programmes and supplier relationships that sit upstream of every bank's own payments procurement — and its annual report PDFs list investments and partners.

source_name: Halcom d.d. – novice / reference (payment & e-banking vendor)
why_relevant: Slovenian-origin payments/e-banking vendor serving, by its own claim, 70+ commercial banks and 4 central banks in nine countries. Vendor news, reference lists and product pages (e.g. MultiPay) are where a won contract is announced when the buying bank stays silent — the classic post-award weak signal.

source_name: Akademija Finance – konference (Finance.si business conference programme)
why_relevant: Finance.si runs the main commercial Slovenian business/IT conference series; agendas and sponsor lists put banks and their vendors on the same stage. Sponsorship itself is a signal — vendors sponsor where they have or want a named account.

source_name: Delo Poslovni Center (dpc.delo.si) – konferenca Mobilne tehnologije / payments panels
why_relevant: Delo's conference arm ran 'Mobilne tehnologije 2026' (Ljubljana, 10 June 2026) with a round table on digital money, digital payments and AI in financial systems — a venue where Slovenian bank and payment-scheme executives describe in-flight platform work.

source_name: Finančna konferenca (financna-konferenca.si)
why_relevant: Long-running Slovenian finance conference (37th edition referenced) with fintech/financing tracks; agenda and partner list identify which fintech and payment vendors are actively courting Slovenian financial institutions.

source_name: ZBS YouTube channel – Bančna konferenca session recordings
why_relevant: Full recordings of the Slovenian Banking Conference are published publicly. Spoken remarks in panels are markedly less filtered than written materials and often name in-flight platform projects that appear in no agenda text.

source_name: Necenzurirano.si – investigative outlet (bank IT failure reporting)
why_relevant: Investigative reporting exposes migrations retrospectively via their failures — e.g. detailed coverage of BKS Bank customers hit by duplicated standing orders and statement errors after an information-system overhaul. Failure coverage confirms a migration happened, when, and often who supplied it, for deals never otherwise disclosed.

source_name: NLB – Javni razpisi (public calls page)
why_relevant: Discovered while mapping NLB's hiring footprint: a first-party page where the bank publishes its own calls. Bridges this indirect cell back to the direct-procurement workstream for the largest SI bank.
